basis: Round-8 live re-check of the R6-08-A residual on 2026-10-17. (2) The round-6 limit that 'other qere and reception legs ... remain unquoted' is addressed with fresh quoted passages from the entry's own cited reference work: the JE 'YHWH' section (Masorites inserted the vowels of Adonai 'indicating thereby that Adonai was to be read (as a "ḳeri perpetuum") instead of Yhwh'; 'Jehovah' is 'a philological impossibility'), the JE 'The Name' section ('it was known in the earliest rabbinical works simply as the Name'; Temple-priests/Adonai-outside sentence citing Soṭah vii. 6), and the JE 'Ehyeh-Asher-Ehyeh' section ('no trace of knowledge as to the pronunciation of the Name' after the Second Temple's destruction). (3) The translation layer was retrieved separately (mishnah.org, entry-cited; Sefaria API with version metadata), so the Hebrew primary text, the reference-work paraphrase, and the English translation are distinguishable layers. All retrieval receipts carry URLs, HTTP 200 statuses, byte counts and sha256 hashes of the fetched artifacts (commands in retrieval_method and negative_sweeps). The entry itself is byte-unchanged (sha256 f25a4b4066f6172afc697a279854ee85ed8a01ee1efdf00097e1d418ed1e80aa, identical to the round-6 baseline).
limits: Retained and new limits. (1) The Hebrew Wikisource page is marked 'לא בדוק' (not proofread) and displays three textual versions with minor variance; the citation is to the displayed standard text, not a named manuscript. (2) All Hebrew/Aramaic glosses in this receipt are this worker's, not Danby's; Danby 1933 was not inspected, and the online expanded English (mishnah.org / Sefaria William Davidson Edition) is a different editorial layer. (3) Jouon-Muraoka 2006, the entry's cited grammar for the pointing-cue claim, remains unread: the entry-cited Google Books ISBN landing page returns only a blurb, which is not a passage. (5) The Mishnah's c. 200 CE dating (entry line 112) is not re-verified by any passage retrieved this round. (6) Nothing retrieved recovers an Iron Age pronunciation or supports a universal ancient ban; the entry does not claim either, and JE's 'no trace' sentence is a denial of transmitted reading, not of scholarly reconstruction proposals.
